chapterTitle: The One-Upmanship Strategy: Give Your Rivals Enough Rope to Hang Themselves
coreMove: Recognize when a rival is already damaging itself and avoid the attack that would unify or rescue it; let the burden of its own choices create the opening you inherit.
reversal: The strategy fails when the operator mistakes passivity for judgment or waits while the rival stabilizes, recovers, or harms the field beyond repair.
teachingEmphasis: treat one-upmanship as restraint rather than flashy sabotage
show how attacks can rescue a failing rival by creating unity
teach successor positioning without romanticizing passivity
name the limit where waiting becomes complicity or drift
